title: A Normal Guy Plays Dark Souls - Part 1 - Intro Through Taurus Demon
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r6_PIKzQJ8Q

Daniel (@dungeondive) opens a new casual let's play under the Digital Dive banner, and the framing is right there in the title: he is not a speedrunner, not a no-hit challenge runner, and he promises plenty of embarrassing deaths. What he offers instead is a player who loves this game talking through *why* while he plays it. He rolls a hunter for the starting bow and armour, takes the master key, and commits to a claymore build — light armour, fast roll, one enormous weapon.

The commentary is where the value sits. Daniel makes a strong case for Dark Souls as a masterclass in level design: the Asylum Demon glimpsed through bars long before you can fight it, items placed in sightlines to pull you off the critical path, the ladder-kick shortcut that folds the Undead Burg back onto itself. He praises FromSoftware's refusal to tutorialise — you begin the game already playing it, with nearly every verb available from the first minute — and argues the architecture and atmosphere still outclass the studio's later, smoother work. He also notes the irony that playing carefully is often harder than simply running past everything.

Along the way: a suicide run through New Londo for the Firekeeper Soul, Petrus of Thorolund's stashed evidence of treachery, jolly cooperation with Solaire, and the Taurus Demon dispatched with gold pine resin and a plunging attack. Two episodes are planned; more depends on the numbers.

----

Daniel argues Dark Souls teaches you entirely through play rather than tutorials — does that design philosophy translate to tabletop games, or do rulebooks make it impossible?
